name: Zambia
summary: Zambia has no capital gains tax, no wealth tax and no inheritance, estate or gift tax. Gains on listed and foreign securities are untaxed; an 8% Property Transfer Tax on value applies instead to Zambian land and unlisted Zambian shares. The weak point for this family is dividends: residents' foreign dividends (and interest) are taxed at progressive rates up to 37%, with a foreign tax credit. Dividends from Lusaka-listed companies are exempt.

regimes.name: Zambian tax resident
regimes.description: Source-based income tax, but residents' foreign dividends and interest are taxable at up to 37%; no CGT, wealth or inheritance tax.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present 183 days or more in a charge year, or present other than for a temporary purpose with a view to establishing residence. Non-citizens need an immigration permit.

capital_gains.summary: Zambia has no capital gains tax. Gains on listed or foreign securities are outside income tax (the Income Tax Act taxes Zambian-source income plus residents' foreign interest and dividends only). Instead, Property Transfer Tax (PTT) of 8% of the value is charged, normally on the seller, on transfers of Zambian land and buildings and of shares in Zambian-incorporated companies other than shares listed on the Lusaka Securities Exchange (LuSE).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No CGT at all. PTT does not apply to LuSE-listed shares or to foreign shares.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: PTT 8% (from 1 January 2025) on land, unlisted Zambian shares (including indirect transfers by a non-resident company holding at least 10%), IP and certain mining rights; 10% on mining licences/rights. PTT is levied on value (realisable value/consideration), not on the gain. Business income (a trade in shares or property) is taxable at income tax rates.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Listed (LuSE) and foreign securities: 0 (no CGT; no PTT on listed or foreign shares). Private business (shares in a Zambian company) and Zambian real estate: 0.08 = 8% PTT on the transfer value, recorded as the rate because it replaces CGT; on a gain smaller than the full value the burden relative to the gain is higher (e.g. 16% of a gain equal to half the value). Foreign real estate: 0.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Profits from a business of dealing in shares or property are business income taxed at up to 37% (individual) or 30% (company).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Gains on foreign assets are not taxed; only foreign interest and dividends of residents are brought into Zambian tax.
open_questions: Whether PTT applies to the transfer of Zambian land or unlisted shares to heirs on death or by gift (and on what value) was not verified.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Zambian companies bear a final 15% withholding tax, but dividends paid to individuals by LuSE-listed companies are exempt. Foreign dividends received by Zambian residents are deemed Zambian-source and taxed at the progressive rates (top 37% above ZMW 110,400 a year), with a unilateral foreign tax credit where no treaty applies.

sources.title: Zambia - Individual - Taxes on personal income

dividends.important_exceptions: Dividend WHT is a final tax for individuals. Exempt: dividends from LuSE-listed companies to individuals, mining-company dividends, and certain farming and vehicle-assembly dividends for five years.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 0 for LuSE-listed shares (the relevant case for a listed portfolio); unlisted Zambian companies 15% final WHT. Foreign: deemed Zambian-source, taxed at the 37% top rate before a credit limited to the Zambian tax on that income (treaty rates where a treaty applies).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% (residents) / 20% (non-residents, reducible by treaty) on dividends from Zambian companies; 0% on LuSE-listed dividends to individuals and on mining dividends.
dividends.treaty_network: More than 20 treaties (Deloitte 2026). No US income tax treaty (not verified from the US list), so US dividends bear 30% US WHT.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 30% CIT; no CGT. A company holding a foreign portfolio would itself be taxed on foreign dividends; not modelled.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth or net worth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local council rates on land and buildings (Ministry of Lands / city councils); PTT on transfers.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax, estate duty, gift or donations tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Property Transfer Tax (8%) may arise when Zambian land or unlisted Zambian shares are transferred; whether transfers to heirs or donees are exempt was not verified. Foreign assets and listed securities are outside PTT.
inheritance.gift_tax: None (no donations tax); PTT on gifts of Zambian land or unlisted shares not verified.
open_questions: PTT treatment of transfers on death and of gifts of Zambian real estate not verified.

residency.tax_residency_test: An individual is resident unless present in Zambia only for a temporary purpose and not with a view to establishing residence; presence of 183 days or more in a charge year (calendar year) always makes an individual resident.

routes.name: Immigration permits (investor, employment, residence)
routes.requirements: All non-Zambians need a permit under the Immigration and Deportation Act; investor and residence permit thresholds were not researched in this pass.

corporate.summary: 30% standard CIT for companies and branches (35% electronic communications; mining and other sector rates differ); 5% turnover tax for small businesses. No CGT; PTT applies to transfers of land and unlisted shares. 15% final WHT on dividends to residents, 20% to non-residents.
corporate.special_zones: Multi-facility economic zones and priority-sector incentives (not researched).

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed. Zambia's 37% tax on foreign dividends exceeds the US rate on qualified dividends, so the Zambian tax would be the binding layer (credit mechanics under US rules not analysed). No US-Zambia income tax treaty (not verified).
